title: Snowden NSA Revelations
summary: Edward Snowden leaks classified NSA documents revealing mass surveillance programs, changing the global conversation about privacy.
narrative: A 29-year-old NSA contractor flies to Hong Kong with a laptop full of classified documents. He meets Glenn Greenwald and Laura Poitras in a hotel room. The Guardian publishes the first story: the NSA is collecting phone records of millions of Americans. Then it gets worse. PRISM. XKeyscore. The NSA is tapping undersea cables, hacking servers, and collecting data from Google, Facebook, and Apple. Snowden becomes the most wanted man in America. He's charged under the Espionage Act.
why_it_matters: Changed the global conversation about surveillance and privacy. Forced tech companies to encrypt everything. Created the modern privacy movement. Snowden became the defining whistleblower of the digital age.
image_caption: Edward Snowden leaks classified NSA documents revealing mass surveillance programs, changing the global conversation about privacy.

title: Bitcoin Hits $1,000
summary: Bitcoin's price surges past $1,000 for the first time, reaching a market cap of $15 billion.
narrative: Bitcoin goes from $13 to $1,000 in one year. The Silk Road gets shut down by the FBI. Bitcoin doesn't die — it moons. Every news outlet runs a Bitcoin story. Your uncle asks you how to buy Bitcoin. Mt. Gox, the biggest exchange, processes 70% of all Bitcoin transactions. It will collapse in February 2014. But for this moment, Bitcoin feels real. The crypto dream seems possible.
why_it_matters: First major price milestone. Brought crypto to mainstream attention. The Mt. Gox collapse that followed became a cautionary tale. The $1,000 price was just the beginning.
image_caption: Bitcoin's price surges past $1,000 for the first time, reaching a market cap of $15 billion.

title: PS4 and Xbox One Launch
summary: Sony PS4 and Microsoft Xbox One launch within weeks of each other, beginning the eighth generation of game consoles.
narrative: Sony and Microsoft launch new consoles in November. The PS4 costs $399. The Xbox One costs $499 and requires Kinect. Microsoft reverses its always-online policy after massive backlash. The PS4 wins the generation on pure power and price. Both consoles have built-in streaming. Twitch becomes huge on PlayStation. Gaming becomes a spectator sport.
why_it_matters: Defined the console generation. Streaming became integral to gaming. The always-online backlash showed consumer power. PlayStation's dominance shaped the industry for a decade.
image_caption: Sony PS4 and Microsoft Xbox One launch within weeks of each other, beginning the eighth generation of game consoles.

title: Oculus Rift Kickstarter
summary: Oculus Rift raises $2.4 million on Kickstarter, igniting the modern virtual reality revolution.
narrative: Palmer Luckey, a 20-year-old with messy hair, posts a Kickstarter for a VR headset. He calls it the Oculus Rift. John Carmack, the legendary game developer, promotes it. The Kickstarter blows past its goal. The dev kit ships to backers in 2013. The demos are mind-blowing. You put on the headset and you're somewhere else. Facebook buys Oculus for $2 billion in 2014. The metaverse is born.
why_it_matters: Revived virtual reality after decades of failure. Created the modern VR industry. Facebook's acquisition made VR a mainstream tech priority.
image_caption: Oculus Rift raises $2.4 million on Kickstarter, igniting the modern virtual reality revolution.

title: Vine Launches
summary: Twitter launches Vine, a 6-second looping video app that creates a new format for short-form video content.
narrative: Twitter buys a tiny app called Vine. It lets you make 6-second looping videos. It's absurdly simple. Kids go crazy for it. The Vine stars become famous: Logan Paul, Jake Paul, Lele Pons. The format is addictive. Six seconds forces creativity. Brands try to make Vines and fail. Teens make Vines that get millions of loops. The 6-second format doesn't survive, but the idea of short-form video is permanent.
why_it_matters: Created the short-form video format. Directly influenced TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts. The Vine star model created the modern influencer economy.
image_caption: Twitter launches Vine, a 6-second looping video app that creates a new format for short-form video content.

title: EA Launches Origin
summary: EA fully launches Origin as its digital distribution platform, challenging Steam's dominance in PC gaming.
narrative: EA pulls its games from Steam and launches its own platform: Origin. Gamers are furious. They don't want another launcher. But EA has FIFA, Battlefield, Madden — games people will install anything to play. Origin is clunky, slow, and has customer service horror stories. It proves that even a bad platform can survive if it has exclusive content. Every publisher learns the lesson: build your own launcher.
why_it_matters: Started the launcher wars. Every major publisher now has their own platform. Showed that content exclusivity drives platform adoption, even when the platform is inferior.
image_caption: EA fully launches Origin as its digital distribution platform, challenging Steam's dominance in PC gaming.

title: Google Glass Explorer Edition
summary: Google ships the Glass Explorer Edition to early adopters, sparking a global debate about wearable technology and privacy.
narrative: Google ships a computer that looks like glasses to 2,000 Explorers for $1,500. They look ridiculous. People call them 'Glassholes.' But the technology is real: heads-up display, voice commands, camera. Bars ban Glass. Restaurants ban Glass. The privacy debate explodes. Google pauses the project. The concept survives — smart glasses, AR, heads-up displays. The execution was just too early.
why_it_matters: Pioneered the smart glasses concept. Sparked the privacy-vs-innovation debate. The backlash influenced how tech companies approach wearable cameras.
image_caption: Google ships the Glass Explorer Edition to early adopters, sparking a global debate about wearable technology and privacy.

title: Yahoo Acquires Tumblr for $1.1 Billion
summary: Yahoo acquires Tumblr for $1.1 billion, promising to 'not screw it up' — and promptly screws it up.
narrative: Marissa Mayer pays $1.1 billion for Tumblr. David Karp stays on as CEO. Mayer promises not to change it. Yahoo adds ads. They try to make it family-friendly. The community revolts. Tumblr's creative, counterculture identity clashes with Yahoo's corporate culture. Karp leaves in 2016. Yahoo gets sold to Verizon in 2017. Tumblr gets sold to Automattic for $3 million. From $1.1 billion to $3 million.
why_it_matters: One of the worst acquisitions in tech history. Showed that buying a community doesn't mean you own it. The $3 million sale price became a cautionary tale.
image_caption: Yahoo acquires Tumblr for $1.1 billion, promising to 'not screw it up' — and promptly screws it up.

title: Black Lives Matter Movement Begins
summary: The #BlackLivesMatter hashtag is created after the acquittal of George Zimmerman, becoming a global movement for racial justice.
narrative: George Zimmerman is acquitted in the shooting death of Trayvon Martin. Alicia Garza writes a Facebook post: 'Black people. I love you. I love us. Our lives matter.' Patrisse Cullors adds the hashtag. #BlackLivesMatter is born. It starts as a social media call. It becomes the largest social movement in American history. The hashtag becomes a rallying cry, a protest sign, a way of seeing the world.
why_it_matters: Created the most important social movement of the decade. Proved hashtags can become real-world movements. Changed how we talk about race and justice.
image_caption: The #BlackLivesMatter hashtag is created after the acquittal of George Zimmerman, becoming a global movement for racial justice.

title: Microsoft Acquires Nokia's Phone Business
summary: Microsoft acquires Nokia's phone business for $7.2 billion, the final nail in the coffin for the world's former phone giant.
narrative: Nokia was the world's biggest phone maker. Then the iPhone happened. Nokia chose Windows Phone. It didn't work. Stephen Elop, the CEO, was a former Microsoft executive. He steered Nokia toward Microsoft's platform. When Microsoft buys Nokia for $7.2 billion, it feels like a betrayal. Nokia's phone business dies slowly. By 2017, the brand is sold to HMD Global. The $7.2 billion write-off is one of the biggest in corporate history.
why_it_matters: End of Nokia's phone empire. One of the worst corporate acquisitions in history. Microsoft's phone business never recovered. The $7.2 billion became a meme about corporate mismanagement.
image_caption: Microsoft acquires Nokia's phone business for $7.2 billion, the final nail in the coffin for the world's former phone giant.

title: Vine Launches & Pioneers 6-Second Comedy Video Culture
summary: Twitter released Vine, where users looped 6-second clips that established short-form comedic video.
narrative: Constrained by an ultra-short six-second limit and seamless looping, Vine creators mastered jump-cuts, slapstick timing, and rapid punchlines. Teenagers made videos in bedrooms that racked up tens of millions of loops, launching stars like Shawn Mendes and David Dobrik. The app became a thriving incubator for Black creative comedy and viral catchphrases ('Do it for the Vine!', 'Yeet!', 'What are those!?').
why_it_matters: Vine invented the rhythm, visual language, and creator culture of short-form vertical video that TikTok and Reels later transformed into an empire.
image_caption: Twitter released Vine, where users looped 6-second clips that established short-form comedic video.

title: Apple Releases iOS 7: The Death of Skeuomorphism
summary: Jony Ive overhauled Apple's interface, replacing leather textures and glossy buttons with neon flat minimalism.
narrative: Gone was the green felt in Game Center, the yellow legal pad in Notes, and the faux leather stitching in Calendar. Jony Ive ushered in frosted translucent blurs, razor-thin typography, dynamic parallax wallpapers, and bold neon color palettes. The tech world gasped in shock, but within months, virtually every mobile app, operating system, and website on earth discarded skeuomorphism in favor of flat digital surfaces.
why_it_matters: iOS 7 represented the most radical and influential design reboot in consumer software history, shaping digital aesthetics for a decade.

title: Daft Punk's 'Get Lucky' & Lorde's Anti-Pop Sensation 'Royals'
summary: French robots Daft Punk revived live disco-funk with Pharrell, while 16-year-old Lorde conquered the world with 'Royals'.
narrative: With Nile Rodgers' sublime rhythmic guitar scratching and Pharrell Williams' falsetto, Daft Punk's 'Get Lucky' from *Random Access Memories* was the inescapable sound of summer. Meanwhile, from suburban Auckland, New Zealand, 16-year-old Ella Yelich-O'Connor (Lorde) dropped 'Royals'—a minimalist bass-and-finger-snap critique of pop star luxury that won Song of the Year and ushered in melancholic, whispery pop.
why_it_matters: These tracks signaled a rebellion against cookie-cutter EDM synths, steering mainstream music back toward organic funk instrumentation and bedroom minimalism.
image_caption: French robots Daft Punk revived live disco-funk with Pharrell, while 16-year-old Lorde conquered the world with 'Royals'.
